aspects.says: When a validate-then-update sequence is copied into several callers, making one copy atomic leaves the other copies racing, with each other and beside the fixed one, while the fixed copy's own load test passes.
basis: section:A Fix Made in One Copy of a Check-Then-Update Leaves the Other Copy Racing

aspects.says: On one thread the unfixed copy behaves correctly at the limit; only concurrent traffic through it shows the race, so a test of the fixed path alone cannot find it.
basis: section:A Fix Made in One Copy of a Check-Then-Update Leaves the Other Copy Racing

aspects.says: With the validate-then-update as one method of the owning class, one edit to that method fixes every caller, mixed traffic included, without changing the callers, and a load test of that method covers them all.
basis: section:A Fix Made in the Owning Class Reaches Every Caller Without Touching Them

aspects.says: The owner's fix holds only while callers cannot reach the state: with the counter private a pasted copy of the sequence fails to compile; a read-only value accessor is safe, an accessor returning the mutable counter reopens the race.
basis: section:The Fix Holds Only While No Caller Can Reach the Counter

aspects.says: getAndUpdate may apply its function more than once under contention, so the function only computes the new value and side effects follow the call.
basis: section:A Fix Made in the Owning Class Reaches Every Caller Without Touching Them
aspects.reason: unit 5.3.2 owns and checks this; here it is one clause, and whether a function is re-applied depends on contention a deterministic test cannot arrange through the reader's code
